# LABEL COVERAGE

Generated by `src/label_coverage.py`. Applies `labels/technique_lookup.yaml` to
every VCDB record. These are **our** labels, not the official VERIS→ATT&CK
crosswalk — see that file's header and `DATA_SURVEY.md` §3.3 for why.

---

## 1. Lookup validation

Technique IDs checked against the pinned ATT&CK bundle (Enterprise 19.2).

All 21 lookup rows validate: every ID exists, none are revoked or
deprecated, and every name matches the canonical ATT&CK name.

## 2. Coverage

| Outcome | Records | % of VCDB |
|---|---|---|
| **Labelled** — a curated variety matched | 2,582 | 24.4% |
| **Excluded** — category has no ATT&CK equivalent | 5,986 | 56.5% |
| **Uncovered** — in-scope category, no curated variety | 2,028 | 19.1% |
| Total | 10,596 | 100.0% |

The labelled pool is **2,582 records** against a target of 400 pairs — a 6.5× surplus, so the dataset can be sampled
selectively rather than scraped together.

### 2.1 Coverage of the cyber-relevant pool

Coverage against all of VCDB understates the result, because most of VCDB is
out of scope by design. The meaningful denominators:

| Denominator | Records | Labelled | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| All VCDB | 10,596 | 2,582 | 24.4% |
| Has a hacking/malware/social action | 4,364 | 2,582 | 59.2% |
| …and at least one named (non-Unknown/Other) variety | 2,714 | 2,582 | 95.1% |

**1,650 records (37.8% of the cyber pool) record only `Unknown` or `Other`** as the action variety.
No lookup can label these — VERIS states that *something* happened without
stating what. They set a hard ceiling on any variety-based labelling scheme.

## 4. Class balance risk

**The distribution is dominated by one class.** `T1486` (Data Encrypted for Impact) accounts
for **1,196 of 2,582 labelled records (46.3%)**. The top
three techniques together account for 73.6%.

The tail is thin as well — 4 of 14 techniques have fewer than 20
records:

- `T1003` (OS Credential Dumping): 4
- `T1105` (Ingress Tool Transfer): 6
- `T1485` (Data Destruction): 11
- `T1041` (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel): 16

**Why this matters.** Sampling 400 pairs proportionally would reproduce this
skew. A model that answers with the majority technique unconditionally would score
well on technique accuracy while performing no analysis at all — and with a single
training run (SCOPE.md §6) there is no second attempt to correct for it.

### Proposed mitigation: per-class cap

Cap each technique at **55 records** when sampling.

*Note:* `src/select_records.py` uses a fixed `CLASS_CAP` of 205, set when the
target was larger. At 400 pairs the global largest-remainder
apportionment does the balancing, so the cap only prevents one class from
monopolising the candidate pool. The realised split is in `DATASET_STATS.md` §2.

| Property | Uncapped | Capped at 55 |
|---|---|---|
| Largest class share | 46.3% | 10.9% |
| Pool available to sample | 2,582 | 504 |

This keeps the pool at 504 records — 1.26× the 400 pairs needed, leaving slack for records later lost to the token budget — while holding every class at or under 25%.

Three further rules for the dataset-build phase:

1. **Floor rare classes.** Techniques with fewer than 20 records should either be
   included in full or dropped entirely — a class present with three examples
   teaches nothing and adds noise to per-class accuracy.
2. **Stratify the train/test split by technique**, so the 40-record
   test set is not accidentally all one class.
3. **Report the majority-class baseline** alongside technique accuracy. Without it,
   the metric cannot be distinguished from guessing the most common label.
